fact: TRACE Strategies, LLC is an operations execution partner.
Consultants leave decks. We create systems.
TRACE does lean transformation and forward-deployed engineering for enterprises and scaling organizations.
Every problem is unique: TRACE does not hand over a textbook answer; it strategizes and builds solutions with the team, not at them.
The TRACE method has five steps: Target, Roadmap, Automation, Cadence, Enterprise.
Target: pin down the handful of targets that actually decide your year. Not forty goals. The few that matter.
Roadmap: turn each target into one visualized roadmap across every program. Sequenced, owned, on a clock you steer.
Automation: find the manual work quietly eating budget and morale, then hand it off. Only where it is safe. Never on blind trust.
Cadence: a sustainable rhythm that keeps the machine moving and turns hindsight into foresight. Humans included.
Enterprise: govern like the biggest do: audit-ready, traceable, investment-planned. Every base covered, at your scale.

Lean transformation means cutting the waste out of how work moves through a business (handoffs, waiting, unplanned rework): map how it really runs, remove steps that do not earn their place, and hand back a tighter version of the same business. Same output, less friction, lower cost.

Forward-deployed engineering means TRACE engineers work inside the operation, build the fix in the real systems, and stay until it runs without them. The difference between advice and a working system installed where the work happens.
TRACE does not replace an existing ops team; it hands them a working system, because most teams know something is broken but lack the bandwidth to rebuild it mid-flight.
This is not AI consulting. AI is a tool used where it earns its place; the product is a fixed operation, and agents are part of how it runs, not the pitch.
TRACE starts with an audit, not a call: you see your own gaps in writing first, so the conversation starts at the fix.
Weeks, not months: scope one highest-leverage fix, install it, and hand it off, so the change is felt fast instead of waiting on a year-long transformation.
Built for owner-led teams that have outgrown the spreadsheet but are not ready for a heavy PMO. If that is not you, TRACE will say so.
The Operations Audit Workbook is free: it walks you through your own operation and shows you the gaps, before you spend a dollar. Get it at tracestrategies.com.
Contact: connect@tracestrategies.com.

The TRACE method moves a business through eight stages and produces twelve deliverables with fixed schemas; each deliverable has an acceptance test that is a running thing, and names its executor (a person, a system, or an agent).
Deliverable A8, the ownership matrix: every capability has one accountable owner, no gaps, no ties; ownership sits alongside where each capability's data lives (stage 4).

A TRACE install runs five steps: Diagnose (audit), Direct (a written operating plan the client keeps), Build (install into their real stack), Run with them (TRACE runs the first stand-ups and planning sessions in the new system with the team), Stay (retainer for the edge cases around week three).
Propose and approve: AI never writes to production on its own; the agent drafts the exact change (tool, project, owner, objective) and nothing is written until a person approves.
